title: Freya and the Parish
premise: Zephyrine Delacroix, the concierge of the Grand Meridian Hotel in the coastal parish of Saint-Aubin, has spent five years quietly cataloging the town's secrets—none more haunting than the disappearance of Freya Okonkwo, the rector's daughter who vanished in 2019. When a guest checks in carrying Freya's diary, its entries continuing two years past the date she supposedly died, Zephyrine realizes the case everyone closed was never closed at all. Following the diary's coded references to parish landmarks, Zephyrine uncovers a smuggling ring protected by the town's most respected families and discovers Freya alive, hiding in plain sight as the parish's anonymous organist. To save her, Zephyrine must choose between exposing the truth through legal channels—which would destroy Freya's fragile new life—and delivering justice outside the law, and the choice costs them their job, their safety, and nearly their heart, before Freya finally chooses to testify, ending the parish's long silence.
about_author: Jonah Dunmore is the pen name of a former night-shift hotel clerk who spent a decade collecting the confessions of strangers at front desks across the Gulf Coast. Freya and the Parish is their second novel, written largely between the hours of midnight and dawn.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Small Sins
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. We meet the concierge mid-shift, watching guests lie with practiced grace, and glimpse the locked drawer of index cards where five years of parish secrets live. The emotional beat is quiet competence masking loneliness; Zephyrine notices everything and is noticed by no one.

chapters.title: Guest 411
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A nervous woman checks in under a false name and asks, oddly, whether the hotel has ever had trouble with 'lost things.' That night Zephyrine finds a leather diary left behind in Room 411—Freya Okonkwo's diary. The beat is the first crack in Zephyrine's ordered world.

chapters.title: Entries Past the End
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Reading by lamplight, Zephyrine discovers the diary continues eighteen months beyond Freya's official disappearance date, written in a hand that grows more frightened. The emotional beat is vertigo: the town's settled grief was built on a lie, and Zephyrine is now holding the evidence.

chapters.title: What the Rector Knew
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, with a flashback to 2019. Zephyrine visits Rector Okonkwo under the pretext of charity arrangements and watches him flinch at his daughter's name. The beat is the first confrontation with power: the rector is grieving, but grief and guilt wear the same face.

chapters.title: The Organist Who Wears Gloves
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Sunday service; Zephyrine studies the parish's faceless organist, whose posture matches Freya's and whose left hand hides a scar the diary mentions. The beat is recognition and terror—Zephyrine realizes Freya may be alive and hiding thirty feet from the pulpit.

chapters.title: Filed Under F
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. In the secret drawer, Zephyrine reassembles five years of cards: missing ledgers, a drowned fisherman, payments routed through the hotel's books. The parish's respectable families ran something out of the harbor, and Freya found out. Beat: dread hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Woman in 411 Returns
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Zephyrine and the guest, Nadia. Nadia is Freya's old friend, hunting the diary's missing second half; she doesn't know Zephyrine has it. Their wary alliance forms over bad coffee. Beat: Zephyrine is no longer alone, and no longer safe.

chapters.title: Someone Ransacks Room 411
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The room is torn apart; the hotel manager, Cormac Bell, orders Zephyrine to stay out of it with a threat wrapped in a promotion. Beat: fear and defiance—the drawer is moved to Zephyrine's apartment, crossing a line that can't be uncrossed.

chapters.title: The Harbor at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and Nadia's POV, alternating. Following diary clues, they search the boathouse where Freya last wrote, finding a hidden ledger of the smuggling operation. They are nearly caught by Bell's men. Beat: the mystery turns physical and dangerous.

chapters.title: A Note in the Hymnal
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. In the organ loft, a hymnal bears a penciled message clearly meant for whoever was clever enough to look: 'Stop before they stop you. —F.' Beat: heartbreak—Freya is protecting the town that abandoned her, and warning Zephyrine away.

chapters.title: The Rector's Confession, Half-Given
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Zephyrine confronts the rector privately; he admits Freya discovered the ledger but swears he doesn't know where she went, and begs Zephyrine to let the dead rest. Beat: pity and fury entwined—Zephyrine realizes the rector may be protecting Freya, or protecting himself.

chapters.title: Bell's Offer
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Cormac Bell offers Zephyrine a lifetime post and a quiet word about 'guests who read other people's mail,' making clear he knows about the diary. Beat: temptation as threat—Zephyrine's whole identity as the keeper of secrets is being turned against them.

chapters.title: Nadia Disappears
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Nadia misses their meeting; her room is emptied, her car gone, a single index card from Zephyrine's own drawer left on the pillow. Beat: cold terror—the enemy has been inside Zephyrine's system all along, and now the hunter is hunted.

chapters.title: The Second Diary
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Decoding the diary's marginal dates, Zephyrine finds Freya's real hiding instructions and a cache beneath the hotel's old chapel floor: the second diary and proof that Bell murdered the fisherman who tried to leave the operation. Beat: the case flips from disappearance to murder.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Organ Loft
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and Freya's POV, finally shared. Zephyrine confronts the organist; Freya, unmasked, tells the truth—she faked her death to escape Bell, and the rector has kept her secret at the cost of his reputation and faith. Beat: the love-against-duty theme ignites; two keepers of secrets recognize each other.

chapters.title: What Justice Looks Like Here
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya argues against going to the police: the sheriff is Bell's brother-in-law, and testimony would kill her and her father. She asks Zephyrine to help her disappear for good. Beat: the impossible choice—love asks Zephyrine to bury the truth they've bled to uncover.

chapters.title: The Sheriff's Long Shadow
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Zephyrine tests the law, anonymously tipping a state investigator, and watches the tip die in the sheriff's inbox within hours. Beat: disillusionment—justice outside the law isn't a fantasy here; it's the only door left open.

chapters.title: The Bell Tolls Wrong
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Bell, tipped off by the sheriff, corners Zephyrine in the hotel's service tunnels with a choice: hand over the diaries or join Nadia, whose fate he implies with a smile. Beat: the darkest hour—Zephyrine surrenders the diaries to save time, not themselves.

chapters.title: The Plan in the Drawer
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and Freya's POV, converging. Zephyrine reveals they kept photographic copies and had already mailed them to a state journalist and the investigator's supervisor. Freya, furious and moved, agrees to one condition: she'll testify only if her father hears the truth from her first. Beat: resolve forged from ruin; duty and love briefly aligned.

chapters.title: The Rector's Sermon
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Sunday service; Freya plays the organ through a final hymn, then stops the service and speaks. The rector, weeping, stands beside her as she names Bell from the pulpit. Beat: the climax—secrets detonated in the one place the parish cannot look away from.

chapters.title: Handcuffs in the Nave
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. State troopers, tipped by the journalist's calls, arrest Bell at the church door; the sheriff is suspended by afternoon. Nadia is found alive, held in a coastal cabin. Beat: catharsis—justice arrives late, outside the town's law but not outside the larger one.

chapters.title: The Concierge Who Noticed Everything
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Months later: Zephyrine, no longer at the Grand Meridian, keeps a small guesthouse where Freya, publicly restored, visits under her own name. The drawer of index cards is burned; some things should be remembered by people, not files. Beat: resolution—love chosen over duty, and a life finally lived unalphabetized.
